domain_restrictions: d is a nonnegative integer (so affine d-space and the polynomial ring have d variables; includes the special case d = 0)
each weight w_i is a positive integer
I is homogeneous with respect to the weighted grading determined by deg(x_i) = w_i
the zero-locus condition is stated after base change to an algebraic closure of k, so points are taken in affine d-space over k_bar
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For all fields k, all nonnegative integers d, all positive integer weights w_1 through w_d, and all ideals I in S = k[x_1,...,x_d] that are homogeneous for the weighted grading, if the variety over an algebraic closure k_bar has common zeros exactly at the origin in affine d-space, then the quotient ring S/I has finite dimension as a vector space over k.
quantifier_order: for all positive integer weights w_1,...,w_d
for all weighted-homogeneous ideals I of S = k[x_1,...,x_d]
if over k_bar the common zero locus of I in affine d-space equals exactly the origin
then S divided by I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space

statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=w_i. Let I be a homogeneous ideal of S. If, over an algebraic closure of k, the common zero locus of I in affine d-space is exactly the origin, then S/I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space.
